q: Is the manufacturing licence (Form 25/28) valid, displayed, and does it cover every section and dosage form we make?
why: Making any drug outside the licence is treated as manufacture without licence.
law: Drugs & Cosmetics Act s.18(c); Drugs Rules r.70–76
evidence: Licence copy + latest retention fee receipt

q: Is every product, strength and pack we make endorsed on the approved product list?
why: An unapproved product can be seized and the batch destroyed.

q: Are the approved manufacturing chemist and analytical chemist the same people named on the licence, and present daily?
why: Inspectors first check the technical staff. A missing person can suspend the licence.

q: Is a complete Batch Manufacturing Record signed for every batch and kept safely?
why: No record means the batch legally does not exist. This is the most common inspection failure.

q: Is every raw material and packing material tested and released by QC before use?
why: Untested material is the main cause of 'not of standard quality' cases.

q: Is every finished batch tested and released by QC, with control samples kept?
why: A failed sample in the market leads to prosecution of the proprietor.
law: Drugs Rules r.74, r.78; Schedule M
evidence: Batch release register + control sample log

q: Do all labels carry name, batch, Mfg/Exp date, licence number, MRP and the correct Schedule H/G warning?
why: A wrong label makes the drug 'misbranded' even if quality is perfect.

q: Have we checked whether any of our brands need a QR code / barcode on the label?
why: Listed brands sold without the QR code are treated as misbranded.

q: Is the revised Schedule M gap assessment done and are all gaps being closed with dates?
why: Revised Schedule M applies to every unit from 1 Jan 2026. Inspections are risk-based now.

q: Is a yearly Product Quality Review prepared for each product?
why: It is a compulsory Schedule M document and inspectors ask for it.

q: Is internal self-inspection done as per a yearly plan, with a report?
why: It finds problems before the inspector does.

q: Is there a written recall procedure and was a mock recall done in the last 2 years?
why: On a quality failure we must be able to pull back stock fast.

q: Is every market complaint entered in a register and investigated?
why: Ignored complaints become legal cases.

q: Is a pharmacovigilance officer named and are side-effect reports sent to PvPI?
why: This is now a licence condition under Schedule M.

q: Can we show batch-wise where every batch was sold?
why: Needed for recall and asked for in every sampling case.

q: Is the inspection book (Form 35) available and are all past inspection remarks closed in writing?
why: Open remarks from the last visit are the first thing checked in the next one.

q: For any third-party or loan-licence manufacturing, do we hold the signed agreement and the other party's valid licence?
why: We remain responsible for the product sold under our name.

q: Are the licences and daily stock registers for NDPS / controlled substances complete and tallied?
why: NDPS shortage or excess is a criminal offence with jail.

q: Is the excise permit for rectified spirit / ethanol valid and does the stock register tally?
why: Excise shortage brings heavy penalty and can stop supply.

q: Are wholesale licences 20B and 21B valid, displayed and is the retention fee paid?
why: Selling drugs with a lapsed licence is an offence.

q: Is the competent person named on the licence working with us and present?
why: Sale without the competent person breaks the licence condition.

q: Do we buy only from licensed manufacturers/dealers and keep every purchase bill for 3 years?
why: The purchase bill is our only defence if a drug is found spurious.

q: Do we sell only to licensed dealers, hospitals or doctors and keep a copy of each buyer's licence?
why: Sale to an unlicensed party is punishable.

q: Does every sale invoice show batch number, expiry, manufacturer name and both parties' licence numbers?
why: Incomplete invoices are noted as violations in inspections.

q: Are storage temperatures recorded daily, with a working fridge and log for 2–8°C products?
why: Wrong storage spoils the drug and the dealer is held liable.

q: Are expired and damaged goods kept separately, marked 'Not for sale' and returned or destroyed with a record?
why: Expired stock on the sale shelf is an offence even if not sold.

q: Do the premises match the approved plan, and was any change in premises or constitution informed to FDA?
why: An unreported change can cancel the licence.

q: Is the cosmetics licence (COS-8) valid, displayed, and does it cover every category we make?
why: Making a category not on the licence is manufacture without licence.

q: Are all ingredients checked against the BIS list of banned and restricted substances and permitted colours?
why: A banned ingredient makes the product illegal to sell.

q: Do labels show name, maker's address, net content, batch, Mfg date, use-before date, ingredients and licence number?
why: Label errors are the top reason cosmetics fail on Amazon and in inspections.

q: Are labels and ads free of medical claims (cures, treats, heals)?
why: A medical claim turns the cosmetic into an unlicensed drug.
law: D&C Act s.3(aaa), s.3(b); Cosmetics Rules r.36

q: Is a batch record kept for every batch, with raw materials tested before use?
why: Required under cosmetics GMP and asked for at every inspection.

q: Are the approved technical staff the same as named on the licence?
why: Staff mismatch can suspend the licence.

q: Are finished products tested to the BIS standard (including heavy metals and microbial limits) and records kept 3 years?
why: A failed market sample leads to prosecution.

q: Is every new product within licensed categories, with the product list given to FDA where required?
why: Keeps the licence and the actual product range matched.

q: Do we hold a Free Sale Certificate / product documents for each export market?
why: Shipments get stuck at the buyer's port without them.

q: Are the ONDLS / SUGAM portal logins active and linked to the owner's email and mobile (not an agent's)?
why: All licences now run on these portals. Losing the login stops every application.

q: Before launching any new formula, do we check if it is a 'new drug' or FDC needing CDSCO approval first?
why: A state licence alone is not enough for a new drug. Penalty is severe.

q: Has our product list been checked against the latest list of banned drug combinations (FDCs)?
why: Making a banned FDC is an offence from the date of the ban.

q: Has every 'Not of Standard Quality' notice been answered and the batch recalled?
why: Unanswered notices go straight to court.

q: Are WHO-GMP and CoPP certificates valid for the products we export?
why: Buyers and tenders reject expired certificates.

q: Do we hold CDSCO import registration and licence (Form 10 for drugs / COS-2 for cosmetics) before importing?
why: Customs will not release the goods without it.
law: Drugs Rules r.23–27; Cosmetics Rules r.12–13

q: Is the MRP of every scheduled (NLEM) product at or below the NPPA ceiling price, updated each April?
why: Overcharging is recovered with interest plus penalty.

q: For other products, was the MRP raised by not more than 10% in the last 12 months?
why: NPPA tracks this and demands the excess back.

q: Is a current price list (Form V) issued to dealers and filed with NPPA?
why: A missing price list is a separate violation.

q: Is the firm registered on NPPA's IPDMS portal with product data up to date?
why: Quarterly and yearly NPPA forms can only be filed there.

q: Before launching a new strength or combination of a scheduled drug, do we take NPPA retail price approval (Form I)?
why: Launch without price approval means the whole sale value can be treated as overcharge.

q: Before stopping any scheduled product, do we give NPPA 6 months' notice (Form IV)?
why: NPPA can order us to keep making it.

q: Is the manufacturer's price list available at our wholesale counter?
why: Dealers must show it on demand.

q: Are all instruments and balances calibrated as per a schedule, with stickers?
why: An uncalibrated instrument makes every test result doubtful.

q: Are stability studies running for every product to support the shelf life on the label?
why: Shelf life without data is treated as a false claim.

q: Is the purified water system validated and is water tested regularly (chemical and microbial)?
why: Water is the biggest hidden source of contamination.

q: Are process and cleaning validations done for each product?
why: Required by revised Schedule M.

q: Are changes, deviations and failed results (OOS) recorded and investigated?
why: Inspectors look for honest records of problems, not zero problems.

q: Do we buy materials only from an approved vendor list?
why: Bad suppliers cause most quality failures.

q: Are GMP training records and yearly medical fitness certificates kept for production staff?
why: Both are compulsory and easy to miss.

q: Are computer and instrument records protected (individual logins, no deleting, backups)?
why: Data integrity failures lead to the strictest action.

q: Is pest control done on schedule with records?
why: Simple to do, always checked.

q: Are reference standards and lab chemicals within validity?
why: Expired standards make test results invalid.

q: Was Consent to Establish taken before setting up or expanding the unit?
why: Building first and applying later invites closure and environmental compensation.
law: Water Act s.25; Air Act s.21

q: Is Consent to Operate (Air and Water) valid, and is production within the products and quantity allowed in it?
why: Running without valid consent can shut the unit and cut power.
law: Water Act s.25–26; Air Act s.21

q: Is the effluent treatment plant running daily with a logbook and lab test reports of treated water?
why: A switched-off ETP is the most common reason for PPCB closure orders.

q: Are stack, DG set and ambient air/noise tests done as the consent requires?
why: Consent conditions are checked at renewal.

q: Is hazardous waste authorisation valid, waste stored under 90 days, recorded (Form 3) and sent only to an authorised facility with manifests?
why: Illegal disposal brings personal liability on the owner.

q: Is bio-medical waste from the lab handed to the authorised collector, with agreement and records?
why: Applies to microbiology labs and first-aid rooms.

q: Is the firm registered on the CPCB plastic EPR portal and are yearly recycling targets met?
why: Unregistered brand owners cannot legally sell in plastic packaging.

q: Is there permission for the borewell, with a water meter fitted?
why: Unpermitted borewells can be sealed.

q: Does the DG set have an acoustic enclosure and correct stack height?
why: Standard consent condition.

q: Was the yearly environment statement (Form V) filed and are consent fees paid?
why: Late filing delays consent renewal.

q: Are old computers, batteries and tube lights given only to authorised recyclers?
why: Applies to every office, even without a factory.

q: Is the factory licence valid and does it cover the actual number of workers and power load?
why: Under-declared workers or load is a common penalty.

q: Is the factory building plan approved by the Director of Factories, with a stability certificate?
why: Needed for the licence and for insurance claims.

q: Are the required registers kept (workers, attendance, overtime, leave, accidents)?
why: Missing registers are fined per register.

q: Are first-aid boxes stocked, with trained first-aiders on each shift?
why: Checked in every safety inspection.

q: Are lifts, hoists and pressure vessels tested by a competent person on time?
why: An accident on untested equipment is a criminal case.

q: Are all machines guarded and is safety gear (PPE) issued with a record?
why: Most factory injuries come from unguarded machines.

q: Is there a written procedure to report accidents to the Factory Inspector in time?
why: Not reporting an accident is punished separately.

q: Is overtime within legal limits and paid at double rate?
why: A frequent labour-court claim.

q: Are drinking water, toilets, rest room (and canteen if required) provided and clean?
why: Basic welfare items every inspector looks at.

q: Are safety data sheets available for all chemicals, with an emergency plan?
why: Needed for worker safety and fire response.

q: Are the required notices displayed (working hours, holidays, abstract of the Act, inspector's name)?
why: Small fine, easy to avoid.

q: Is the boiler registered and is its yearly inspection certificate valid?
why: Running an uncertified boiler is illegal and very dangerous.

q: Is the boiler run only by a certified boiler attendant?
why: Required by law and by insurers.

q: Are air receivers, autoclaves and other pressure vessels tested and tagged?
why: Vessel failure causes serious injury.

q: Is the PESO licence valid for solvent storage / gas cylinders, and is storage within the licensed quantity?
why: Excess storage voids insurance and risks an explosion case.

q: Is the autoclave validated and its safety valve tested?
why: Needed for both GMP and safety.

q: Is the fire safety certificate (Fire NOC) valid for the premises?
why: Without it, insurance may refuse a fire claim.
law: Punjab Fire and Emergency Services Act 2024

q: Are fire extinguishers refilled and tagged, and hydrants/hose reels tested?
why: An empty extinguisher is useless on the day it is needed.
law: National Building Code; Fire NOC conditions

q: Was a fire drill held in the last 6 months, with a record?
why: People must know the way out.
law: Fire NOC conditions; Factories Act s.38

q: Are exits clear, with exit signs, emergency lights and a working alarm?
why: Blocked exits cause the deaths in a fire.

q: Is wiring checked yearly and is the solvent store fitted with flameproof fittings?
why: Short circuit is the top cause of factory fires.

q: Does fire insurance cover building, machines and stock at today's value?
why: Under-insurance cuts every claim in the same ratio.

q: Is every eligible employee covered under PF, with UAN and KYC complete?
why: PF dues are recovered with interest and damages for past years.

q: Is every eligible employee covered under ESI and registered before joining work?
why: If an uncovered worker has an accident, the employer pays everything.

q: Are all workers paid at least the latest Punjab minimum wage for their category?
why: Punjab revises rates twice a year. Underpayment is recovered up to 10 times.

q: Are wages paid by the 7th of the month through bank, with wage slips?
why: Cash wages are hard to prove later.

q: Does every employee have a signed appointment letter?
why: Now compulsory, and the best defence in a dispute.

q: Are combined registers kept (employees, wages, attendance, leave)?
why: First thing a labour inspector asks for.

q: Is yearly bonus paid on time and recorded?
why: Applies to eligible employees once the firm has 20 or more.

q: Is gratuity liability known and paid within 30 days of leaving?
why: Delay carries interest.

q: Is there a POSH Internal Committee with an outside member, a displayed policy and yearly report?
why: Fine of ₹50,000 and possible licence action if missing.

q: Do contractors hold a valid licence and do we check their PF/ESI challans every month?
why: If the contractor defaults, the principal employer pays.
law: OSH Code 2020 (contract labour); EPF Act s.8A

q: Is the office / shop registered or intimated under the Punjab Shops Act?
why: Needed for bank, GST and labour records.
law: Punjab Shops & Commercial Establishments Act 1958 (as amended)

q: Is age proof kept for every worker, with nobody under 18 in production?
why: Child labour is a non-bailable offence.

q: Is Punjab Labour Welfare Fund deducted and deposited?
why: Small amount, checked in inspections.

q: Are apprentices engaged in the required band and registered on the portal?
why: Mandatory for 30 or more workers.

q: Are workers not covered by ESI protected by an accident / compensation insurance policy?
why: One serious accident can cost many lakhs.

q: Are maternity benefit and equal pay rules followed?
why: Covers leave, pay and no discrimination.
law: Social Security Code 2020; Code on Wages 2019

q: Is the GST certificate displayed and are all offices, godowns and factories added as places of business?
why: Goods lying at an unregistered godown can be seized.

q: Is the GSTIN shown on the name board at every place?
why: Fine up to ₹25,000.

q: Is an e-invoice (IRN) made for every B2B sale, and an e-way bill wherever needed?
why: An invoice without IRN is not a valid invoice, so the buyer loses credit.

q: Is input tax credit matched with GSTR-2B every month, and reversed where suppliers are unpaid beyond 180 days?
why: Wrong credit is the biggest source of GST notices.

q: Are HSN codes and GST rates correct for every product after the latest rate changes?
why: A wrong rate means tax, interest and penalty on all past sales.

q: Is reverse-charge GST paid on transport, legal fees and similar items?
why: Often missed and picked up in audit.

q: Are books, invoices and stock records kept for 6 years?
why: Department can ask for any of these years.

q: Is the Letter of Undertaking (LUT) renewed every April before the first export?
why: Without it, IGST must be paid on exports.

q: Are job-work goods sent on challan and tracked until return?
why: Goods not back in time are treated as a sale.

q: Does someone check the GST portal every week for notices?
why: Notices come only online, and replies have short time limits.

q: Are expired-goods returns handled with correct credit notes / ITC reversal?
why: A special rule for pharma that is often done wrongly.

q: Are the income-tax and TDS portal logins linked to the owner's own email and mobile?
why: Notices and OTPs must reach us, not an old accountant.

q: Is TDS deducted on every payment where it applies (salary, contractors, rent, professionals, purchases)?
why: Missed TDS means the expense is disallowed, plus interest.

q: Are cash payments above ₹10,000 a day to one person avoided, and no cash of ₹2 lakh or more received?
why: The expense is disallowed and a 100% penalty applies on receipts.

q: Are micro and small suppliers paid within 45 days?
why: Unpaid amounts are added to taxable income for the year.
law: Income-tax Act (former s.43B(h)); MSMED Act s.15

q: Is advance tax worked out and paid each quarter?
why: Avoids interest.

q: Does someone check the income-tax portal every week for notices?
why: Faceless notices have short reply times.

q: Are sales, purchases and loans between the four Velite firms billed at fair price and documented?
why: Related-party dealings are the first thing examined in scrutiny.

q: Is a fixed asset register kept with bills?
why: Supports depreciation and insurance claims.

q: Does the HUF have its own PAN, bank account and separate books?
why: Mixing HUF and personal money weakens the HUF's tax status.

q: Are statutory registers kept (members, directors, charges, loans)?
why: Asked for by banks, investors and ROC.

q: Are board meetings held as required with signed minutes?
why: Missing meetings bring a penalty on every director.

q: Is the auditor properly appointed and ADT-1 filed?
why: Accounts cannot be validly signed otherwise.

q: Are director KYC and digital signatures valid?
why: A deactivated DIN blocks all filings.

q: Do the name board, letterhead and invoices show company name, CIN and registered office?
why: Penalty per day of default.

q: Are loans from directors and relatives backed by declarations and reported in DPT-3?
why: Money from others can be treated as illegal deposits.

q: Are dealings with the other Velite firms approved by the board and entered in the register?
why: Directors are personally liable for unapproved related-party deals.

q: Is every bank loan charge registered with ROC within 30 days?
why: Late filing costs heavy extra fees.

q: Are share certificates issued and stamped, and is the beneficial-owner declaration in place?
why: Proves ownership clearly.

q: Is the Import Export Code active and updated this year (April–June)?
why: A de-activated IEC stops all shipments.

q: Is the export council membership (RCMC) valid?
why: Needed for incentives and many buyers.

q: Is the bank AD code registered at every port we use and is ICEGATE login working?
why: Shipping bills cannot be filed otherwise.

q: Are shipping bills matched with bank realisation, and RoDTEP / drawback claimed?
why: Unclaimed incentives are lost money.

q: Do export packs follow the export labelling rule and the buyer country's registration?
why: Wrong labels are rejected at the foreign port.

q: Before each export, is the product checked against restricted lists (SCOMET, NDPS, CITES)?
why: Restricted items need a licence.

q: Are bills of entry, duty payments and required NOCs (CDSCO / BIS / FSSAI) kept for every import?
why: Records can be audited for 5 years.

q: Are any Advance Authorisation / EPCG export obligations tracked with dates?
why: Unmet obligations mean duty plus interest.

q: Is payment for every export received within 15 months and the bank's EDPMS entry closed?
why: Old open entries put the exporter on the caution list.

q: Do all foreign payments (including Amazon Global) come through the bank or an RBI-approved payment route?
why: Money through informal routes is a FEMA violation.

q: Where a buyer paid in advance, was the shipment made in the agreed time?
why: Bank monitors unshipped advances.

q: Is any discount, write-off or reduction of export invoice value routed through the bank?
why: It cannot be adjusted on our own.

q: Are import payments made as per contract and IDPMS entries closed with the bill of entry?
why: Open entries block future import payments.

q: For any foreign investment, was FC-GPR filed within 30 days and is the FLA return filed by 15 July?
why: Late filing needs compounding with RBI.

q: Is the firm registered as packer / manufacturer under Legal Metrology?
why: Selling packed goods without registration is fined per pack type.

q: Does every pack show maker's name and address, product name, net quantity, month/year, MRP (incl. all taxes), customer-care contact and country of origin?
why: The most common reason for fines and Amazon listing removal.

q: Is net quantity checked during packing and within allowed tolerance?
why: Short weight is a criminal offence.

q: Are all weighing scales and measures verified and stamped on time?
why: Unstamped scales are fined on the spot.

q: Is the MRP never raised with a sticker, and are price changes made only on new packs?
why: Sticker over a lower MRP is an offence.

q: Do online listings show the same compulsory details as the label?
why: Applies to Amazon and our own website.

q: Has the company nominated a director as the responsible person?
why: Otherwise all directors are liable.

q: Is the FSSAI registration / licence valid, in the right category for our turnover and activity (wholesaler, distributor, retailer)?
why: Selling food without it: fine up to ₹10 lakh. Wrong category is also a violation.

q: Is the FSSAI number printed on our invoices and the Food Safety Display Board put up?
why: Compulsory on every food bill.
law: FSSAI order on invoices; licence conditions

q: Do we buy food products only from FSSAI-licensed makers and keep a copy of their licence?
why: The trader shares liability for unsafe or unlicensed food.

q: Do the food packs we sell carry full labels (FSSAI logo and number, veg mark, best-before, ingredients, nutrition)?
why: A seller can be fined for mislabelled food on his shelf.

q: Are our food products and ads free of disease or cure claims, with approvals for any health supplement?
why: Health supplements and nutraceuticals have strict claim rules.

q: Is food stored clean, pest-free, apart from drugs and chemicals, with expired stock kept separately?
why: Schedule 4 hygiene rules apply to traders too.

q: Have we confirmed in writing whether the yearly FSSAI return (Form D-1, by 31 May) applies to our licence type?
why: It is for makers, repackers, relabellers and importers. If we relabel or repack, it applies to us.

q: Has one supervisor done FSSAI food-safety training (FoSTaC)?
why: Expected for licensed businesses.

q: Is the land allowed for our use (industrial zone / focal point allotment, or Change of Land Use permission)?
why: This is the one approval that cannot be fixed later with a fee.
law: Punjab Regional & Town Planning Act 1995; Master Plan Ludhiana

q: Is the building plan sanctioned by the right authority (GLADA, Municipal Corporation, PSIEC or Director of Factories)?
why: Unsanctioned buildings can be sealed and block every other licence.
law: Punjab Urban Planning & Development Building Rules 2021

q: Does the building match the sanctioned plan, with any extra construction regularised (compounded)?
why: Mismatch surfaces at loan, sale or licence renewal time.

q: Do we hold a completion / occupancy certificate for the building?
why: Needed for bank loans, fire NOC and sale.

q: Are EDC, CLU and other development charges fully paid, with receipts?
why: Dues carry interest and block no-dues certificates.

q: Is the title deed or lease registered in the correct firm's name and are allotment conditions met?
why: The plot must stand in the name of the firm that holds the licences.

q: Is there a registered rent deed that allows our type of use, with the landlord's building approvals on file?
why: Most licences ask for a registered deed.

q: Before any new construction or expansion, do we take all approvals first (through Invest Punjab single window)?
why: For the new VS plant: approvals first, then construction.

q: Is the sanctioned load / contract demand enough for all machines actually connected?
why: PSPCL is penalising use beyond sanctioned limits.

q: Is the maximum demand on each monthly bill checked against contract demand?
why: Exceeding it adds a demand surcharge every month.

q: Before adding any new machine, do we apply to PSPCL for load extension?
why: Unauthorised load is charged as penalty with back-billing.

q: Is each electricity connection in the correct firm's name and tariff category (industrial / commercial)?
why: Wrong category leads to back-billing under 'unauthorised use'.

q: Is the power factor kept healthy with a working capacitor bank?
why: Poor power factor raises the kVAh bill.

q: Is Chief Electrical Inspector approval in place for the HT installation, transformer and DG set?
why: Mandatory before energising, and needed for insurance.

q: Are earthing and electrical safety tests done yearly by a licensed contractor?
why: Prevents shocks and fires.

q: Are electricity bills paid on time and the security deposit kept updated?
why: Avoids surcharge and disconnection.

q: Is there a list of every plant, animal or marine-origin ingredient we use, with its source?
why: This list decides which of the rules below apply.

q: Has prior intimation been given to the Punjab Biodiversity Board for commercial use of Indian biological resources, with benefit-sharing paid if due?
why: Boards have raised demands on cosmetics makers for past years. Cultivated plants are largely exempt, so check each ingredient.

q: Do suppliers of herbal extracts and oils give a declaration of origin (cultivated or wild, Indian or imported)?
why: This is our proof if the Board asks.

q: Have we confirmed that no ingredient comes from a protected species (Wildlife Act schedules or CITES list), such as sandalwood, agarwood or kuth?
why: Use or export without a permit is a criminal offence.

q: For exports containing listed plant species, is the CITES / legal procurement certificate obtained?
why: Shipment will be held at customs.

q: For raw herbs or forest produce bought directly, is the forest transit permit on file?
why: Applies only if we buy raw produce, not finished extracts.
law: Indian Forest Act 1927; Punjab transit rules

q: Is the municipal trade licence valid for each premises inside city limits?
why: Needed for many other registrations.

q: Is property tax paid up to date?
why: Arrears carry penalty and block no-dues certificates.

q: Do all vehicles have valid registration, insurance, pollution certificate and fitness?
why: Insurance will not pay if any paper has lapsed.

q: Are insurance policies in force for stock, building, machinery, goods in transit and public liability?
why: One uninsured loss can undo years of profit.
law: Policy terms; Public Liability Insurance Act 1991

q: Is Udyam (MSME) registration updated with the latest turnover and investment?
why: Protects our right to 45-day payment and bank benefits.

q: Are bank stock statements, insurance and limit renewal papers given on time?
why: Delay brings penal interest.

q: Are originals of all licences, deeds and approvals kept in one safe place, with scanned copies?
why: Saves days during inspections, loans and renewals.

q: Are digital signature tokens kept by the owner, not with outside consultants?
why: A DSC can sign anything in our name.

q: Are water and sewer connections approved and bills paid?
why: Checked for no-dues certificates.

q: Do we follow the pharma marketing code: no gifts, trips or cash to doctors, with records of samples and events?
why: Yearly self-declaration by the head of the firm is required.

q: Are all ads, leaflets and social-media posts free of banned claims (cure of listed diseases, magic remedies)?
why: Punishable with jail, and now watched closely by courts.
law: Drugs & Magic Remedies Act 1954; Schedule J

q: Is there a signed agreement and a valid drug licence copy for every distributor and stockist?
why: Supply to an unlicensed party is our offence too.

q: Do online listings show seller name and address, country of origin, MRP and a grievance contact?
why: Marketplaces delist non-compliant products.

q: Are Amazon brand registry, category approvals and product documents kept current?
why: A suspended account stops sales overnight.

q: Is the customer-care number / email on our packs working and are complaints answered?
why: Unanswered complaints go to consumer court.

q: Is every brand name registered as a trademark in the correct firm's name, with renewals tracked?
why: An unregistered brand can be copied or even claimed by others.

q: Before using a new brand name, do we check it is not similar to an existing drug brand?
why: FDA asks for an undertaking with every new product.

q: Are third-party manufacturing, supply and distributor agreements signed, stamped and filed?
why: An unsigned agreement is hard to enforce.

q: Do we collect customer and employee personal data with a clear notice and consent?
why: Penalties under the new data law are very high.

q: Are websites and domain names owned in the firm's name with terms and privacy pages?
why: Domains in an employee's or agency's name are a real risk.

q: Is there one register of all court cases and government notices with next dates?
why: A missed hearing can mean an ex-parte order.

q: Do key staff have confidentiality terms for formulas and customer lists?
why: Protects know-how when people leave.
